lessons.title: Health tips and home remedies
lessons.goal: Give and pass on health tips with the du, ihr and Sie commands, sollen and dürfen, and name common home remedies.

grammar.point: A tip can be a command (du, ihr, Sie) or passed on with sollen; ask with Wie oft? and Wie lange?; pick the right pattern: command, soll, darf, nicht dürfen or nicht müssen.
grammar.oneLine: Trink Tee mit Honig! Du sollst im Bett bleiben. Wie oft soll ich die Tablette nehmen?

mistake.why: After sollen the second verb is an infinitive and goes to the end; the command form is only for commands.

terms.meaning: a home remedy, such as tea with honey
a short piece of advice
a long word made from smaller words

cards.title: Before we start: health tips
cards.body: Your friend has a cold. What can you tell her? You can give a tip as a command, or pass it on with sollen. Today you put everything from this chapter together and learn a few home remedies.
steps: You already know: Trink viel Tee (du command), Du sollst im Bett bleiben (sollen), both from this chapter
New today: choose the right pattern for a tip: command, soll, darf, nicht dürfen or nicht müssen
By the end you can: give health tips in three ways and ask Wie oft? and Wie lange?

examples.en: Drink a lot of tea. (to a friend)
examples.why: You know this already. The du command.

examples.en: You are supposed to stay in bed.
examples.why: You know this already. Passing on advice with sollen.
New today: a home remedy, Honig, in a tip.

cards.more: This lesson is a toolbox day. You already have three tools for advice: the command, sollen and darf. Today you learn when to pick which one, like choosing between a hammer and a screwdriver. You also meet some household remedies, and you add Wie oft? and Wie lange? to ask how often and how long. You will learn this step by step in the next cards.

cards.title: Give a tip three ways
cards.body: You can give the same tip in three ways. A command to a friend (du): Trink Tee! A polite command (Sie): Trinken Sie Tee! Or pass it on with sollen: Du sollst Tee trinken. Choose by who you speak to and who said it.

examples.en: You are supposed to drink a lot of tea.

steps: du command: Trink viel Tee!
Sie command: Trinken Sie viel Tee!
sollen: Du sollst viel Tee trinken.
cards.more: The tip is the same, only the packaging changes. Step 1: who are you talking to? A friend: du command. A stranger: Sie command. Step 2: did somebody else say it? Use soll. In a command the verb is first. With sollen the modal is in part 2 and the verb goes to the end. Extra example: Schlaf viel! Schlafen Sie viel! Du sollst viel schlafen.
cards.lead: You know sollen, dürfen and the command forms. Next: three ways to give the same health tip, so you can choose the right form for who you talk to.

deeper.text: A command is direct. Du sollst sounds as if you pass on someone else's wish, so it feels less pushy. Between friends, the command is normal and quick. When you want to be gentler, or you repeat a doctor's words, use sollen. Same advice, different tone.

example.en: You are supposed to drink water.

cards.title: Household remedies in Germany
cards.body: Many Germans first try a Hausmittel (a home remedy). Typical ones: Hühnersuppe or Tee mit Honig for a cold, Kamillentee for a stomach ache, Zitrone in hot water. A Hausmittel is not a Medikament. With a high fever, go to the doctor.
cards.more: Every family has a grandmother with her own medicine cabinet. In Germany it is full of tea: Kamillentee for the stomach, Tee mit Honig for the throat. For a cold there is hot Hühnersuppe, and some people even put a warm Zwiebel on a sore ear. These are Hausmittel: home remedies. They help a little, but with a high fever you still go zum Arzt. Step 1: learn the table. Step 2: make a du command: Trink Kamillentee! Extra example: Iss Hühnersuppe! = Eat chicken soup!
cards.lead: You can give a tip in three ways. Next: home remedies in Germany, so you can name a common remedy like tea with honey.

deeper.text: Tee mit Honig has no article after mit. That is allowed when you mean the thing in general. If you say mit dem Honig, you mean the honey, one particular jar, and the article takes the dative. So no article is a simple and normal way to describe a drink or a dish.

cards.title: How often? nie, manchmal, oft, immer
cards.body: Four small words tell how often. nie = never. manchmal = sometimes. oft = often. immer = always. They stand after the verb: Ich rauche nie. Er joggt oft. At the start of the sentence the verb is still part 2: Manchmal habe ich Kopfschmerzen.

examples.why: Time first: verb is still part 2.

cards.more: Picture a line from 0 to 100. Nie is at 0. Manchmal is in the middle on the low side. Oft is high. Immer is at 100. Step 1: choose the point on the line. Step 2: put the word after the verb. Step 3: or start with it, and keep the verb in part 2. Extra example: Ich trinke immer Tee. = I always drink tea.
cards.lead: You can name remedies. Next: four small words for how often, nie, manchmal, oft and immer, so you can say how often you do something.

deeper.text: nie already means not ever, so never add nicht. A German sentence has only one negative: Ich rauche nie, not Ich rauche nie nicht. English has the same rule in careful speech. The word nie goes after the verb, like the other frequency words oft and immer.

cards.title: Ask and answer: Wie oft? Wie lange?
cards.body: Ask Wie oft? for how often and Wie lange? for how long. Answer with einmal, zweimal, dreimal am Tag or with drei Tage, eine Woche. These questions fit with dürfen and sollen: Wie oft soll ich die Tropfen nehmen? Wie lange darf ich nicht arbeiten? die Sprechstunde = consultation hours.

examples.en: How often should I take the drops?

examples.de: Wie lange darf ich nicht arbeiten?
examples.en: How long may I not work?

examples.de: Sie sollen zweimal am Tag Tee trinken.
examples.en: You are supposed to drink tea twice a day.

cards.more: Two question words, two kinds of answers. Wie oft? is about the number of times. Wie lange? is about the length of time. Step 1: choose the question word. Step 2: put the modal in part 2. Step 3: the infinitive goes last. Step 4: answer with a number of times (zweimal am Tag) or a length (eine Woche). Extra example: Wie oft soll ich Tee trinken? Dreimal am Tag.
cards.lead: You can say how often. Next: asking Wie oft? and Wie lange?, so you can ask how often to take the drops and how long to rest.

deeper.text: Wie plus another word asks a question about that word: Wie oft? is how often, Wie lange? is how long, Wie viel? is how much, Wie alt? is how old. Learn the pattern wie + word, and you can form many questions on your own without a new word.

example.en: How often do you have a headache?

cards.title: Guess words from their parts
cards.body: A new long word is often two known words. Kamillentee is a tea. Hausmittel is a remedy used at home. Hustensaft = Husten + Saft: a syrup for a cough. Use the pieces and the rest of the sentence to guess. Then check the meaning.

examples.why: Kamille + Tee: it is a tea.
Haus + Mittel: a remedy from the house.

steps: Look for words you know inside the long word.
Read the rest of the sentence: nehmen, trinken, Suppe give hints.
Guess the meaning, then check it.
cards.more: You do not need to know every word. Look inside it. Hustensaft: you know Husten and you know Saft. Together: a juice for the cough. The verb helps too: nehmen suggests medicine, trinken suggests a drink. Step 1: find the small words. Step 2: use the verb as a clue. Step 3: guess. Step 4: check it in your vocabulary list. Extra example: Halstablette = Hals + Tablette: a throat tablet.
cards.lead: You can ask about how often and how long. Next: guessing new long words from their parts, so you can understand words like Hustensaft.

deeper.text: The last piece of a long word gives the article and the basic meaning. der Tee gives der Hustentee, a tea for coughs. Sometimes the first piece takes a little glue sound, as in Ohr and Ohrenschmerzen. It looks long, but you will know every piece, so you can guess the meaning.

cards.title: Which pattern do I need?
cards.body: Look at what you want to say and pick the pattern. Tell a friend what to do: du command. Tell a stranger: Sie command. Pass on an order: sollen. Ask permission: Darf ich …? Forbidden: nicht dürfen. Not necessary: nicht müssen.

examples.en: You do not have to get up.

cards.more: A chef picks the right tool for each job. You pick the right pattern. Step 1: ask yourself: who is speaking, and what do I want? Step 2: look up the pattern in the table. Step 3: fill in the words. Every pattern puts the verb in the first or second place, and a second verb goes to the very end. Extra example: Darf ich anrufen? = May I call?
cards.lead: You can guess new words. Next: choosing the right pattern for what you want to say, so you can pick the command, sollen or dürfen quickly.

deeper.text: Doctors often soften a command with sollen or make it stronger with müssen. Nehmen Sie die Tablette is a normal instruction. Sie sollen die Tablette nehmen sounds like a reminder of what was agreed. Sie müssen die Tablette nehmen means there is no choice. Listen for the verb: it tells you how serious the doctor is.

example.en: You have to take the tablet.

Step 2: see how the verb sits: first in a command, second with a modal, and the infinitive at the end. Step 3: say each line aloud. Extra example: Leon, du darfst morgen aufstehen. = Leon, you may get up tomorrow.
cards.lead: Last card of this chapter: Leon is ill and his friends give him tips, so you can read a real dialogue and see every pattern from the chapter in use.

deeper.text: After sagen you put a colon, and then the quoted sentence starts with a capital letter: Mira sagt: Bleib im Bett. This is how you write what someone said in direct speech. In speech you pause a little after sagt. The sentence after the colon is a complete sentence by itself.

Seine Schwester kauft ein. Leon sagt: Danke, ihr seid super! Dann trinkt er Tee und schläft. Das ist gut für die Gesundheit.

listening.title: Mira ruft Ben an
listening.script:
Mira: Hallo Ben! Wie geht's?
Ben: Nicht gut. Ich habe Fieber.
Mira: Darf ich dich besuchen?
Ben: Ja, bitte! Aber ich soll im Bett bleiben.
Mira: Was soll ich mitbringen?
Ben: Ich soll viel Tee trinken. Ich habe keinen Tee.
Mira: Gut. Ich bringe Tee mit Honig und Hühnersuppe.
Ben: Super, danke! Ich soll dreimal am Tag eine Tablette nehmen.
Mira: Wie lange musst du im Bett bleiben?
Ben: Bis Montag. Ich darf nicht arbeiten.
Mira: Ruf Leon an! Er hat heute Zeit.
Ben: Ja, mache ich. Danke, Mira!
Mira: Gute Besserung, Ben!
